title: GraphLAMA: Enabling Efficient Adaptation of Graph Language Models with Limited Annotations

problem.claim: Graph language models need efficient adaptation to unseen graphs and tasks when only a few labeled examples are available.

gap.claim: In-context learning on graphs has effectiveness and efficiency issues, while instruction tuning requires large amounts of labeled data that can be difficult to obtain.

contributions.claim: GraphLAMA introduces an extra parameter adaptation stage for tailoring graph language models to unseen graphs and tasks with few labeled examples.

GraphLAMA uses a graph neural network with hop encodings and gating modules to transform nodes into the representation space of LLM tokens, enabling task instructions to combine node and language tokens.
GraphLAMA pre-trains non-LLM parameters on node matching, node classification, and link prediction, then updates only a few pre-trained parameters during few-shot adaptation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report state-of-the-art performance on few-shot and zero-shot node classification and summary generation, with a 4.91% absolute improvement in accuracy.
The authors report inference speed up to 10 times faster than in-context learning under a 5-shot setting.
The authors state that their code is available on GitHub.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph language models extend large language models to graph analysis and can support natural-language task interpretation and few-example learning.
Existing in-context learning has graph effectiveness and efficiency limitations, while instruction tuning depends on difficult-to-obtain labeled data.
The paper proposes an efficient few-shot parameter adaptation stage and introduces GraphLAMA with a specialized backbone and learning schemes.
GraphLAMA maps graph nodes into LLM token representations, combines node and language tokens, pre-trains across graph tasks, and adapts a small set of parameters.
The authors report performance improvements, faster inference than in-context learning, and public code availability.

source_observation.claim: Few-shot adaptation updates only a few pre-trained parameters after broader multi-task pre-training.

interpretation.claim: Separating general knowledge acquisition from lightweight task adaptation may reduce annotation and inference costs.

application.claim: For graph tasks with limited labels, consider pre-training reusable graph-to-token representations followed by parameter-efficient adaptation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach transfers to graph settings, tasks, or label regimes beyond those evaluated.

source_observation.claim: The reported inference speed is 10 times faster than in-context learning under a 5-shot setting.

interpretation.claim: Parameter adaptation may reduce the runtime burden associated with long in-context prompts.

application.claim: When deployment latency matters, compare lightweight adaptation against prompt-based graph language model inference.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the hardware, latency measurement procedure, or comparison conditions beyond the 5-shot setting.

unknowns: Evaluated datasets, dataset sizes, and task-specific data splits are not specified.
Baselines, statistical variation, and detailed experimental protocols are not specified.
